hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: APOE4/4 microglia produced significantly less fluorescence from a lysosomal degradation substrate than APOE3/3 cells, although reduced substrate uptake could contribute.
rows.Finding quote: Since cathepsins play an essential role in lysosomal degradation, we further analyzed lysosomal activity in iMGs using flow cytometry with an Abcam’s proprietary self-quenched substrate and found that E4/E4 iMGs exhibited significantly lower lysosomal degradation activity compared to E3/E3 cells (Fig. 1G-H). Bafilomycin-treated cells served as a negative control (Fig. 1I). Lysosomal degradation activity can be influenced by the efficiency of substrate uptake into endosomes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (lower lysosomal substrate degradation signal)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia under basal conditions; Abcam ab234622 self-quenched substrate incubated for 1 hour; FITC-channel mean fluorescence measured by flow cytometry.
rows.Data location: Fig. 1H; gating in Fig. 1G and APOE3/3 bafilomycin control in Fig. 1I

rows.Finding description: After Aβ42 exposure, APOE4/4 microglia had significantly more galectin-1 puncta than APOE3/3 cells, indicating greater lysosomal membrane damage.
rows.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 4F, H, the formation of galectin puncta, detected with galectin (LGALS)-1-specific antibody, was significantly higher in E4/E4 iMGs than in E3/E3 iMGs after Aβ42 exposure, indicating increased lysosomal leakage in E4/E4 iMGs.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4 under Aβ42) -> (greater lysosomal membrane permeabilization)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 200 nM soluble Aβ42 oligomer preparation for 48 hours; LGALS1 immunostaining and confocal galectin-puncta assay. Puncta were normalized to nuclei; the Methods reports three images per line per treatment, not the number of lines.

rows.Finding description: Bafilomycin-based LC3-II:LC3-I measurements showed no significant difference in basal autophagic flux between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
rows.Finding quote: As expected, blocking autophagic flux by inhibiting lysosomal acidification with bafilomycin A led to increased LC3-II: LC3-I ratio compared to the basal levels (Fig. 1C, D), but there was no significant difference between the genotypes.
rows.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was detected in basal autophagic flux.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; basal cultures compared with bafilomycin A1 treatment for 3 hours; immunoblot LC3-II:LC3-I ratios used to assess autophagic flux.

rows.Finding description: Rapamycin-induced autophagic-flux measurements showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
rows.Finding quote: Similarly, treatment with rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTORC1 complex and a well-known autophagy inducer, did not reveal any significant differences between the genotypes (Fig. 1C, E).
rows.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was detected in rapamycin-induced autophagic flux.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 100 nM rapamycin for 6 hours, with or without bafilomycin A1; LC3 immunoblotting and LC3-II:LC3-I ratios.

rows.Finding description: LAMP2 protein tended to be lower in APOE4/4 than APOE3/3 microglia, but the text does not establish a significant genotype difference.
rows.Finding quote: Interestingly, lysosomal-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP-2), a key mediator of autophagosome-lysosome fusion [57, 58], was unaffected by Aβ42 stimulation but tended to be reduced in E4/E4 iMGs (Fig. 4D, E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (trend toward lower LAMP2 protein)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; basal and 48-hour 200 nM soluble Aβ42 conditions, with bafilomycin conditions also shown; LAMP2 immunoblotting. LAMP2 abundance is a surrogate for lysosomal content/fusion capacity, not a direct fusion measurement.

rows.Finding description: Basal proteomics comparing two mutually isogenic APOE4/4 lines with APOE3/3 lines found lower MFSD1 protein, a lysosomal-content surrogate.
rows.Finding quote: Since proteomic analysis comparing two (isogenic to each other) E4/E4 lines to E3/E3 lines revealed a downregulation of two other lysosomal proteins MFSD1 and GLMP in E4/E4 iMGs at basal conditions (Fig. 3B, Table S4), the overall lysosomal protein content may be reduced by E4/E4 genotype.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (lower basal lysosomal MFSD1 protein)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived microglia under basal conditions; DIA-PASEF LC-MS/MS proteomics. Two APOE4/4 lines were isogenic to each other; this does not establish that the entire APOE4/4-versus-APOE3/3 comparison was isogenic. Sample size 2 counts the reported APOE4/4 lines only.

rows.Finding description: Aβ42-associated LC3-II accumulation showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
rows.Finding quote: Further, we analyzed LC3-II levels by WB, and found that, similarly to LPS/IFNγ stimulation, Aβ42 strongly increased intracellular LC3-II (p = 0.04), irrespective of the APOE genotype (Fig. 4B, C).
rows.Finding summary: Aβ42 increased LC3-II, with no significant genotype difference reported.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 200 nM soluble Aβ42 oligomer preparation for 48 hours; LC3-II immunoblotting. The preparation contained measurable endotoxin.

rows.Finding description: Under basal conditions, human APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia had significantly lower LC3-II protein levels than APOE3/3 cells, a surrogate that does not itself establish impaired lysosomal degradation.
rows.Finding quote: Under basal conditions, E4/E4 iMGs exhibited significantly lower LC3-II levels compared to E3/E3 cells (Fig. 1A, B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (lower basal LC3-II in human iPSC-derived microglia)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived microglia from multiple APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 lines, including an isogenic pair; unstimulated cultures; LC3 immunoblotting. The study-wide eight APOE3/3 and six APOE4/4 lines are not a panel-specific sample size. Available donor ages include 63–80 years; cellular aging was not experimentally established.
rows.Data location: Fig. 1A,B; corresponding uncropped LC3 blots in supplementary PDF pages 1–3, 6, 8–9

rows.Finding description: After 48 hours of LPS/IFNγ stimulation, LC3-II accumulation showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
rows.Finding quote: Consistent with the proteomics data, this WB analysis confirmed that 48-h stimulation with LPS/IFNγ strongly increased the accumulation of LC3-II as well as glutamine synthetase (GLUL), although the protein levels were not affected by the APOE genotype (Fig. 3C, D).
rows.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was reported in LC3-II accumulation after LPS/IFNγ.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 50 ng/ml LPS plus 15 ng/ml IFNγ for 48 hours; LC3-II immunoblotting in an experiment independent of the proteomics.

rows.Finding description: Blocking endosome maturation and degradation with apilimod increased dextran accumulation in both APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia; the legend reports N=3 iPSC lines.
rows.Finding quote: Moreover, when endosome maturation and degradation were blocked by apilimod, a significant accumulation of dextran was observed over 24 h, irrespective of the APOE genotype (repeated measures ANOVA, time x treatment p < 0.001, Fig. 1M).
rows.Finding summary: Apilimod increased dextran accumulation irrespective of APOE genotype. P < 0.001 applies to time × treatment.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 0.683 µM apilimod versus DMSO vehicle; pHrodo-dextran fluorescence accumulation reported over 24 hours. The legend's N=3 iPSC lines does not specify allocation by genotype.

rows.Finding description: Basal pHrodo-dextran fluorescence accumulated less in APOE4/4 than APOE3/3 microglia over time, but this assay cannot separate reduced uptake from altered acidification.
rows.Finding quote: To assess pinocytosis (fluid-phase endocytosis), we added pHrodo-conjugated dextran (MW 10 kDa) and monitored intracellular fluorescence over 20 h using the IncuCyte live imaging system (Fig. 1J, K). Under basal conditions, pinocytosis was significantly reduced in E4/E4 iMGs compared to E3/E3 iMGs (two-way repeated measures ANOVA, time x genotype p = 0.01; Fig. 1J, L).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (lower basal pHrodo-dextran signal in endolysosomal compartments)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; basal exposure to 10 kDa pHrodo-dextran at 16.7–20 µg/ml; IncuCyte fluorescence monitoring over 20 hours, normalized to cell confluence. This is an uptake/acidic-compartment surrogate, not a calibrated lysosomal-pH assay.
rows.Data location: Fig. 1J,K; Results associates the longitudinal test with Fig. 1J,L, whereas the legend assigns the time-course quantification to K

rows.Finding description: Under basal conditions, TOM-20 protein showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia, providing an indirect mitochondrial-mass/mitophagy readout.
rows.Finding quote: Under basal conditions or after treatment with bafilomycin A, there were no differences in TOM-20 protein levels between the genotypes (Supplementary Fig. 2C).
rows.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was reported in basal TOM-20.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; basal cultures; TOM-20 immunoblotting as a mitochondrial-mass surrogate used by the authors to assess mitophagy.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig. 2C; supplementary raw-blot PDF pages 2–3

rows.Finding description: After rapamycin treatment, mitochondrial mass assessed through TOM-20 showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
rows.Finding quote: Similarly, treatment with rapamycin, with or without bafilomycin A, did not reveal any differences in mitochondrial mass between the genotypes, suggesting similar levels of mitophagy (Supplementary Fig. 2D).
rows.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was reported in TOM-20-assessed mitochondrial mass after rapamycin.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 100 nM rapamycin for 6 hours; TOM-20 immunoblotting as an indirect mitochondrial-mass/mitophagy readout.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig. 2D; supplementary raw-blot PDF pages 4–5, 7

rows.Finding description: Uptake of pHrodo-conjugated zymosan-coated beads showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia, although this acid-dependent uptake signal is only an indirect lysosomal surrogate.
rows.Finding quote: Interestingly, the APOE genotype did not significantly affect the uptake of pHrodo-conjugated zymosan-coated beads (Supplementary Fig. 2E-G) or fibrillar Aβ42 (Supplementary Fig. 2H, I).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (no change in pHrodo-zymosan uptake signal)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; pHrodo-conjugated zymosan-coated bead uptake assay. The supplied text does not specify panel-by-panel content, incubation duration or biological sample size. Uptake and phagolysosomal acidification are unresolved.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: After organoid-debris challenge, APOE33 microglia acidified from approximately pH 5.15 to 5.05, whereas APOE44 microglia failed to acidify; three wells per condition were imaged.
rows.Finding quote: While baseline LE/Ly pH did not differ between APOE33 and APOE44 iMG (∼5.15), APOE33 iMG exhibited further acidification upon challenge (∼5.05), whereas APOE44 iMG failed to do so (Figure 3G).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (impaired adaptive late-endosomal/lysosomal acidification after organoid-debris challenge)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia challenged with organoid debris; ratiometric ApHID/Alexa 647 dextran imaging; three wells per condition and nine frames per well. Challenge duration, donor age and AD status were not stated.

rows.Finding description: APOE44 microglia had reduced DQ-BSA-measured lysosomal degradation capacity compared with APOE33 microglia; three wells per group were imaged with nine frames per well.
rows.Finding quote: Consistently, lysosomal degradative capacity, assessed by DQ-BSA, was reduced in APOE44 iMG (Figure 3H)56,57.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (lower lysosomal degradation capacity)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; DQ-BSA mean fluorescence intensity per punctum. The panel includes conditions with and without 10 nM bafilomycin, but the Results do not specify the inhibitor condition for the reported genotype difference. Assay duration, donor age and AD status were not stated.

rows.Finding description: In the female UCI5 isogenic APOE33/APOE44 comparison, APOE44 microglia failed adaptive lysosomal acidification and instead alkalinized after organoid-debris challenge; three wells per condition were imaged.
rows.Finding quote: Upon challenge with organoid debris, UCI5 APOE44 iMG lysosomes failed to mount an adaptive acidification response and instead shifted toward alkalinization (Figure 7M).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (impaired adaptive lysosomal acidification, with alkalinization after challenge)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived microglia from the additional female UCI5 isogenic APOE33/APOE44 pair; untreated and organoid-debris-challenged conditions; ratiometric ApHID/Alexa 647 dextran imaging of late-endosomal/lysosomal acidity; three wells per condition, 25 frames per well. Donor age, AD status and challenge duration were not stated.

rows.Finding description: Untreated APOE33 and APOE44 microglia showed no significant difference in baseline late-endosomal/lysosomal pH, reported as approximately 5.15 in both groups; three wells per genotype were imaged.
rows.Finding quote: While baseline LE/Ly pH did not differ between APOE33 and APOE44 iMG (∼5.15), APOE33 iMG exhibited further acidification upon challenge (∼5.05), whereas APOE44 iMG failed to do so (Figure 3G).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (no change in baseline late-endosomal/lysosomal pH)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; untreated baseline; ratiometric late-endosomal/lysosomal pH imaging using dextran-bound ApHID and pH-independent Alexa 647; three wells per genotype and nine frames per well. Donor age, AD status and loading duration were not stated.
rows.Data location: Fig 3G, untreated APOE33 versus untreated APOE44

rows.Finding description: APOE44 microglia had significantly greater BODIPY/LysoTracker colocalization than APOE33 microglia, indicating increased lysosomal neutral-lipid accumulation; two wells per genotype were sampled with nine frames per well.
rows.Finding quote: To assess this possibility, we quantified colocalization of BODIPY and LysoTracker and found that APOE44 iMG have significantly more neutral lipid accumulation in the lysosomes (Figure 3E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (higher lysosomal neutral-lipid accumulation in human microglia)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived microglia from the male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 pair, identified as Jackson Laboratory JIPSC001000/JIPSC001150; baseline culture; BODIPY-493/503 and LysoTracker Red DND-99 colocalization area normalized to LysoTracker area. Donor age, AD status and assay duration were not stated.

rows.Finding description: Representative BODIPY/LysoTracker images accompany the reported greater lysosomal neutral-lipid accumulation in APOE44 versus APOE33 microglia, but the supplementary images themselves were unavailable.
rows.Finding quote: To assess this possibility, we quantified colocalization of BODIPY and LysoTracker and found that APOE44 iMG have significantly more neutral lipid accumulation in the lysosomes (Figure 3E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (higher lysosomal neutral-lipid accumulation)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; representative BODIPY-493/503, LysoTracker Red DND-99 and colocalization images; legend specifies a 50 µm scale bar. Donor age, AD status and imaging duration were not stated.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig S3B; representative images corresponding to Fig 3E assay

rows.Finding description: Of 84 identified lysosomal hydrolases and V-ATPases, 53 were significantly downregulated in APOE44 versus APOE33 microglia; the underlying proteomic dataset used three wells per genotype.
rows.Finding quote: Of the 84 identified lysosomal hydrolases and V-ATPases, 53 were significantly downregulated in APOE44 iMG, supporting lysosomal impairment (Figure S3D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (lower abundance of numerous lysosomal hydrolases and V-ATPases)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; baseline proteomics intersected with a lysosomal enzyme annotation set. Counts describe proteins rather than biological replicates; underlying proteomics comprised three wells per genotype. Donor age and AD status were not stated.

rows.Finding description: Electron microscopy identified instances of electron-dense, concentrically whorled lysosomes in APOE44 microglia compared with APOE33, consistent with lysosomal lipid accumulation.
rows.Finding quote: As an orthogonal approach to visualize lysosomes, we performed transmission electron microscopy on iMG from APOE3 and APOE4 donor lines. Indeed, we found instances in which lysosomes from APOE44 appeared more electron dense, with a concentric, whorled membranous structure, indicative of lipid buildup (Figure 3F).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (lysosomal ultrastructure consistent with increased lipid accumulation)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived microglia described specifically for this experiment as APOE3 and APOE4 donor lines; Fig 3F identifies APOE33/APOE44 groups; transmission electron microscopy of lysosomes. Specific donor lines, donor age, AD status and culture duration were not stated for this experiment.

rows.Finding description: APOE44 microglia had lower HEXA protein abundance than APOE33 microglia in proteomics using three wells per genotype; enzyme activity was not measured.
rows.Finding quote: These data were in agreement with our scRNAseq results, also indicating that lysosomal and endosomal pathways were being downregulated (i.e., LAMP1, LAMP2, HEXA, HEXB) (Figures 3I-K, S3C, Table S6).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (lower lysosomal HEXA protein abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; baseline whole-cell proteomic HEXA abundance; three wells per genotype. Donor age, AD status and culture duration were not stated.

rows.Finding description: Cross-pair proteomic analysis reported reduced lysosomal proteins in KOLF APOE44 versus APOE33 microglia despite limited overall concordance with UCI5; KOLF proteomics used three wells per genotype.
rows.Finding quote: Nevertheless, both lines at the proteomic level show an increase in MHC Class II response and inflammatory response and a decrease in lysosomal proteins (Figure S7I).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44 in KOLF) -> (lower lysosomal protein abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; genotype-associated protein fold changes compared with the female UCI5 pair and analyzed for shared functional enrichment; three wells per genotype in KOLF source proteomics. Donor age and AD status were not stated.

rows.Finding description: APOE44 microglia had higher p62/SQSTM1 protein abundance than APOE33 microglia in three wells per genotype, consistent with autophagosome accumulation but without direct autophagic flux measurement.
rows.Finding quote: Further, p62 (SQSTM1) and LC3B (MAP1LC3B2) were both upregulated, supporting a buildup of autophagosomes (Figure S3E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE33 -> APOE44) -> (higher p62 abundance, a surrogate consistent with autophagosome accumulation)
rows.Experimental system: Human male KOLF isogenic APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia; baseline whole-cell proteomic SQSTM1 abundance, without a reported turnover or flux assay; three wells per genotype. Donor age and AD status were not stated.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had lower LysoTracker fluorescence than APOE3 astrocytes, interpreted as impaired lysosomal activity or acidity although this assay did not provide calibrated lysosomal pH.
rows.Finding quote: Moreover, APOE3-expressing astrocytes showed higher lysosomal activity as indicated by higher lysotracker signal compared to APOE4-expressing cells (Fig. 4D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LysoTracker fluorescence in astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-expressing astrocytes of unspecified derivation and age; 60 nM LysoTracker Deep Red for 30 min at 37 °C; washed and trypsinized cells analyzed by flow cytometry; ratio paired t-test.

rows.Finding description: Untreated APOE4 astrocytes had higher p62 levels than APOE3 astrocytes, consistent with impaired autophagic degradation but not establishing flux or a lipid-mediated mechanism.
rows.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 3A, the levels of p62 were significantly higher in APOE4-expressing cells, yet α-synuclein treatment increased the levels of p62 in the APOE3 but not in APOE4 cells in which the levels of p62 were high to begin with.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher basal p62 in astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3- and APOE4-expressing astrocytes previously described in reference 23; derivation, age and genetic matching unspecified; untreated comparison within a 2 h α-synuclein experiment; p62 immunoblot normalized to actin.

rows.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had significantly lower basal LC3-II than APOE3 astrocytes, consistent with altered autophagy although steady-state LC3-II alone does not establish flux.
rows.Finding quote: However, the levels of LC3-II were significantly lower in APOE4 compared to APOE3-expressing astrocytes, and α-synuclein treatment had no effect on LC3-II levels in APOE4 astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower basal LC3-II in astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-expressing astrocytes of unspecified derivation and age; untreated genotype comparison within a 2 h α-synuclein experiment; LC3 immunoblot normalized to actin.

rows.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had a significantly lower LC3-II/LC3-I ratio than APOE3 astrocytes, consistent with altered autophagy but not independently establishing flux.
rows.Finding quote: The LC3-II/LC3-I ratio was significantly higher in APOE3 compared to APOE4-expressing astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LC3-II/LC3-I ratio)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-expressing astrocytes of unspecified derivation and age; genotype comparison in the 24 h MPP+/rapamycin experiment; LC3 immunoblot and LC3-II/LC3-I ratio.

rows.Finding description: Rapamycin-associated reduction of MPP+-elevated p62 was described as more pronounced in APOE3 than APOE4 astrocytes, without a reported genotype-by-rescue interaction test.
rows.Finding quote: Combined treatment of MPP+ and rapamycin reduced p62 levels compared to MPP+ treatment alone in both APOE3 and APOE4-expressing astrocytes, with more pronounced effect on APOE3-expressing cells.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less pronounced rapamycin-associated reduction of MPP+-elevated p62)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-expressing astrocytes of unspecified derivation and age; 0.2 mM MPP+ with or without 100 nM rapamycin for 24 h; genotype comparison of p62 response by immunoblot.
rows.Data location: Fig. 7B, genotype difference in p62 rescue

rows.Finding description: α-Synuclein increased p62 in APOE3 astrocytes but produced no significant change in APOE4 astrocytes with already elevated p62, indicating different genotype-associated responses.
rows.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 3A, the levels of p62 were significantly higher in APOE4-expressing cells, yet α-synuclein treatment increased the levels of p62 in the APOE3 but not in APOE4 cells in which the levels of p62 were high to begin with.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (loss of the α-synuclein-associated increase in p62)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3- and APOE4-expressing astrocytes, control versus 0.5 μM α-synuclein for 2 h within each genotype; p62 immunoblot normalized to actin. The paper does not specify a vehicle.

rows.Finding description: α-Synuclein significantly reduced LC3-II in APOE3 astrocytes but produced no significant change in APOE4 astrocytes, which already had lower LC3-II.
rows.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 3B, α-synuclein treatment significantly reduced the levels of LC3-II in APOE3-expressing astrocytes. However, the levels of LC3-II were significantly lower in APOE4 compared to APOE3-expressing astrocytes, and α-synuclein treatment had no effect on LC3-II levels in APOE4 astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (loss of the α-synuclein-associated decrease in LC3-II)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3- and APOE4-expressing astrocytes, control versus 0.5 μM α-synuclein for 2 h within each genotype; LC3 immunoblot normalized to actin. The paper does not specify a vehicle.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Following CCCP, approximately 55% of autophagosomes in APOE4 astrocytes versus approximately 90% in APOE3 astrocytes were reported fused with lysosomes.
rows.Finding quote: Furthermore, using the tandem LC3-GFP-RFP reporter30, we found that following CCCP treatment, ~90% of autophagosomes in the APOE3 astrocytes were fused with lysosomes, compared to ~55% in the APOE4 astrocytes (Fig. 3c).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower autophagosome maturation/fusion with lysosomes after CCCP)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse APOE3/APOE4 astrocyte lines transiently expressing LC3-EGFP-mRFP; 10 μM CCCP for 4 h; dual-positive versus red-only puncta area analysis; at least 50 cells per treatment. Lipid metabolism was not measured.

rows.Finding description: Chloroquine-sensitive LC3-II turnover after CCCP was lower in APOE4 than APOE3 astrocytes, indicating reduced autophagic flux.
rows.Finding quote: Accordingly, APOE3 astrocytes treated with CCCP combined with chloroquine showed increased accumulation of LC3-II compared to APOE4 astrocytes, indicating higher autophagic flux30 (Fig. 3d).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower autophagic flux after mitochondrial damage)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse APOE3/APOE4 astrocyte lines; 10 μM chloroquine for 48 h with or without 7.5 μM CCCP during the final 24 h; LC3-II difference with versus without chloroquine; n = 3, experimental unit unspecified.

rows.Finding description: Chloroquine caused less mitochondrial p62 accumulation in APOE4 than APOE3 astrocytes, suggesting reduced lysosome-dependent cargo turnover.
rows.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 2a, increased accumulation (differences between CQ treated and untreated cells) of parkin, p62, LC3-II and ubiquitin was observed in the mitochondrial fraction of the APOE3 astrocytes following treatment, suggesting their degradation is reduced in APOE4 astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower chloroquine-sensitive mitochondrial p62 turnover)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocyte lines expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; 10 μM chloroquine for 24 h versus untreated controls; mitochondrial p62 immunoblotting normalized to AIF.

rows.Finding description: Chloroquine increased parkin abundance only in APOE3 astrocytes, suggesting reduced lysosome-dependent parkin degradation in APOE4 astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: Additionally, treatment with chloroquine/MG-132 led to parkin accumulation only in the APOE3 astrocytes (Fig. 4e, f), indicating its reduced mitophagic and proteasomal degradation, respectively, in the APOE4 astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower chloroquine-sensitive parkin degradation)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse APOE3/APOE4 astrocyte lines; 10 μM chloroquine for 24 h versus untreated controls; whole-cell parkin immunoblotting.

rows.Finding description: At 12 μM CCCP, p62 abundance decreased only in APOE3 astrocytes, suggesting reduced p62 degradation in APOE4 astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: In addition, 12 µM CCCP treatment reduced p62 levels only in the APOE3 astrocytes, indicating increased p62 degradation in these cells (Fig. S1b).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less CCCP-associated p62 degradation)
rows.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse APOE3/APOE4 astrocyte lines; 12 μM CCCP for 24 h versus untreated controls; p62 immunoblotting.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: After LPS exposure, APOE4 showed higher ThT-inferred β-sheet content than APOE3, with the legend specifically describing an APOE4 response at 5 μM LPS absent for APOE3.
rows.Finding quote: Notably, rAPOE4 exhibited a higher β-sheet content, both in isolation and when exposed to LPS, compared with the rAPOE3 isoform (Fig. 6C).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher LPS-associated ThT-inferred amyloid-like APOE aggregation)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human APOE3 and APOE4, 5 μM, with E. coli LPS at 5, 10, or 20 μM in 10 mM Tris, pH 7.4; 30 minutes at 37 °C, then 100 μM ThT for 15 minutes; fluorescence readout; four independent experiments.

rows.Finding description: Without LPS, APOE4 showed higher ThT-inferred β-sheet content than APOE3 in the cell-free aggregation assay.
rows.Finding quote: Notably, rAPOE4 exhibited a higher β-sheet content, both in isolation and when exposed to LPS, compared with the rAPOE3 isoform (Fig. 6C).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher baseline ThT-inferred amyloid-like APOE aggregation)
rows.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human APOE3 and APOE4, 5 μM in 10 mM Tris, pH 7.4; untreated baseline samples in a ThT aggregation assay; methods specify 30 minutes at 37 °C followed by 100 μM ThT for 15 minutes; four independent experiments.

rows.Finding description: Mouse macrophages took up significantly more Amytracker-stained LPS-treated APOE4 aggregates than APOE3 aggregates in four independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: Furthermore, the data indicate that uptake by the cells was significantly more pronounced for the LPS-treated E4 isoform when compared with the LPS-treated E3 isoform (Fig. 8A).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater macrophage-associated uptake of APOE aggregates)
rows.Experimental system: Murine RAW 264.7 macrophage cell line, passages 4–7; recombinant human APOE3 or APOE4, 100 nM, with E. coli LPS, 100 nM, and Amytracker 680; mixtures incubated 30 minutes at room temperature before 1-hour cell exposure at 37 °C; fluorescence after washing; no endosomal or lysosomal marker.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: At 12 months, insoluble whole-hemibrain apoE levels appeared higher in APPPS1:E4 mice than APPPS1:E3 mice, but there was no significant difference.
rows.Finding quote: Mice with the APOE4 allele appeared to have higher apoE levels at 12 and 16 months, but the difference was insignificant.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in insoluble whole-hemibrain apoE levels at 12 months)
rows.Experimental system: Whole hemibrains from 12-month-old APPswe/PS1dE9 heterozygous mice homozygous for human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted replacement, C57BL/6 background; sexes pooled; Tper-insoluble material extracted with guanidine hydrochloride and apoE measured using HJ15.6 capture and HJ15.4b detection antibodies; legend reports 3-11 mice/group across this panel; no subcellular localization.

rows.Finding description: At 16 months, insoluble whole-hemibrain apoE levels appeared higher in APPPS1:E4 mice than APPPS1:E3 mice, but there was no significant difference.
rows.Finding quote: Mice with the APOE4 allele appeared to have higher apoE levels at 12 and 16 months, but the difference was insignificant.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in insoluble whole-hemibrain apoE levels at 16 months)
rows.Experimental system: Whole hemibrains from 16-month-old APPswe/PS1dE9 heterozygous mice homozygous for human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted replacement, C57BL/6 background; sexes pooled; Tper-insoluble material extracted with guanidine hydrochloride and apoE measured using HJ15.6 capture and HJ15.4b detection antibodies; legend reports 3-11 mice/group across this panel; no subcellular localization.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Recombinant ApoE4 increased ABCA1 colocalization with LAMP2 compared with ApoE3 in human HeLa cells, indicating altered localization rather than directly measured lysosomal function.
rows.Finding quote: Greater colocalization of ABCA1 with the late endosome marker LAMP2 and lower colocalization with the recycling endosome marker Rab11 were observed in cells treated with rApoE4 compared with rApoE3 ( Fig. 2 ).
rows.Finding summary: (rApoE3 -> rApoE4) -> (greater ABCA1 colocalization with LAMP2)
rows.Experimental system: Human HeLa cells, not brain cells, stably expressing GFP-tagged ABCA1; 0.2 μM recombinant ApoE3 or ApoE4 for 30 minutes; confocal imaging with LAMP2 immunostaining.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: At 8 months, APPPS1:E4 mice had higher frontal cortical LAMP1 immunoreactivity than APPPS1:E3 mice, interpreted as greater lysosomal accumulation, in groups containing 2–8 mice.
rows.Finding quote: Additionally, APPPS1:E4 mice had higher levels of lysosomal accumulation at 8 and 16 months of age compared to APPPS1:E3 mice (Figure 7D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher frontal cortical LAMP1-positive area at 8 months)
rows.Experimental system: Eight-month-old C57BL/6-background mice heterozygous for APPswe/PS1dE9 and homozygous for human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted replacement; sexes pooled; frontal cortical sagittal sections; percentage area of LAMP1 immunoreactivity. LAMP1 accumulation was used to infer lysosomal dysfunction; lipid metabolism, acidification, and degradation were not tested.
